title: Mycology
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian university 400L Mycology curriculum as taught in a Microbiology department (distinct from a Botany department's plant-taxonomy emphasis): fungal cell biology, classification, reproduction, medically important fungi and mycoses, mycotoxins, antifungal chemotherapy, laboratory diagnosis, and industrially important fungi.

questions.question: The main structural polysaccharide of the fungal cell wall is:
questions.explanation: Fungal cell walls are built mainly of chitin (a polymer of N-acetylglucosamine) along with glucans, unlike bacterial peptidoglycan or plant cellulose.

questions.question: Which feature best distinguishes a mold from a yeast?
options: Molds are prokaryotic while yeasts are eukaryotic
Molds grow as multicellular filamentous hyphae while yeasts are typically unicellular and reproduce by budding
Molds lack a cell wall while yeasts have one
Molds cannot be cultured on artificial media
questions.correct_answer: Molds grow as multicellular filamentous hyphae while yeasts are typically unicellular and reproduce by budding
questions.explanation: Molds form branching, filamentous hyphae that aggregate into a mycelium, whereas yeasts are single-celled fungi that usually reproduce asexually by budding or fission.

questions.question: A dimorphic fungus is one that:
options: Produces two types of spores simultaneously
Can switch between a mold form and a yeast form depending on environmental conditions such as temperature
Has two nuclei in every cell
questions.correct_answer: Can switch between a mold form and a yeast form depending on environmental conditions such as temperature
questions.explanation: Dimorphism refers to the ability of certain fungi to exist as a mold (usually at 25°C/environmental temperature) and convert to a yeast form (usually at 37°C/body temperature), a trait linked to virulence in several pathogenic fungi.

questions.question: Which of the following is a classic thermally dimorphic pathogenic fungus?
questions.explanation: Histoplasma capsulatum grows as a mold with tuberculate macroconidia in soil/environment but converts to a small budding yeast form at body temperature, causing histoplasmosis.

questions.question: Aseptate (coenocytic) hyphae with broad, ribbon-like appearance and right-angle branching are characteristic of fungi in the phylum:
questions.explanation: Genera such as Rhizopus and Mucor (Mucoromycota) characteristically have broad, non-septate hyphae with wide-angle branching, a key feature in diagnosing mucormycosis histologically.

questions.question: The sexual spore formed by fusion of two compatible hyphae in the Mucoromycota (e.g. Rhizopus) is called a:
questions.explanation: In Mucoromycota, sexual reproduction involves fusion of gametangia from compatible (+ and -) mating types to form a thick-walled resting zygospore.

questions.question: Ascospores, produced within a sac-like structure called an ascus, are the sexual spores of members of the phylum:
questions.explanation: Ascomycota (sac fungi) are defined by production of ascospores, typically eight per ascus, following meiosis; Saccharomyces and Penicillium belong to this phylum.

questions.question: Basidiospores are borne externally on a club-shaped structure called a basidium in members of the:
questions.explanation: Basidiomycota (club fungi), which include mushrooms and Cryptococcus, produce sexual basidiospores externally on club-shaped basidia.

questions.question: The germ tube test is used in the clinical laboratory to presumptively identify:
questions.explanation: When incubated in serum at 37°C for 2–3 hours, Candida albicans (and C. dubliniensis) forms germ tubes, a rapid presumptive test distinguishing it from most other Candida species.

questions.question: A patient with AIDS presents with meningitis; India ink staining of cerebrospinal fluid reveals encapsulated budding yeast cells. The most likely organism is:
questions.explanation: Cryptococcus neoformans is an encapsulated yeast whose polysaccharide capsule excludes India ink particles, producing a characteristic halo; it is a major cause of meningitis in immunocompromised patients.

questions.question: Septate hyphae showing dichotomous branching at acute (45°) angles in lung tissue biopsy are most suggestive of infection with:
questions.explanation: Aspergillus species produce septate hyphae that branch dichotomously at acute (roughly 45°) angles, in contrast to the broad, non-septate, wide-angle-branching hyphae of the Mucorales.

questions.question: Dermatophyte infections of keratinized tissue (skin, hair, nails), commonly called ringworm or tinea, are typically caused by species of which three genera?
questions.explanation: The dermatophytes belong to three anamorphic genera — Trichophyton, Microsporum and Epidermophyton — which secrete keratinases enabling them to invade skin, hair and nails.

questions.question: Aflatoxin, a potent hepatocarcinogen frequently contaminating poorly stored groundnuts and maize, is produced mainly by:
questions.explanation: Aspergillus flavus (and A. parasiticus) produce aflatoxins, mycotoxins that are potent liver carcinogens and a significant food safety concern in tropical grain and groundnut storage.

questions.question: Ergot alkaloids, historically responsible for outbreaks of ergotism from contaminated rye, are produced by:
questions.explanation: Claviceps purpurea, a fungal parasite of rye and other cereals, produces ergot alkaloids that cause ergotism (vasoconstriction and hallucinations) when contaminated grain is consumed.

questions.question: Which mycotoxin class, produced mainly by Fusarium species, is a common contaminant of maize and is associated with esophageal cancer risk in some populations?
questions.explanation: Fumonisins, produced chiefly by Fusarium verticillioides and related species, contaminate maize and have been epidemiologically linked to esophageal cancer and neural tube defects.

questions.question: Sabouraud dextrose agar is widely used for primary isolation of fungi in the laboratory mainly because:
options: Its high sugar content and acidic pH (around 5.6) favour fungal growth while inhibiting most bacteria
It contains blood, which fungi require for growth
It selects specifically for dermatophytes only
It is the only medium fungi can grow on
questions.correct_answer: Its high sugar content and acidic pH (around 5.6) favour fungal growth while inhibiting most bacteria
questions.explanation: Sabouraud dextrose agar has a relatively low pH and high glucose concentration, conditions tolerated by most fungi but that suppress the growth of many bacteria, making it useful for selective fungal isolation.

questions.question: Potassium hydroxide (KOH) wet mount preparation is used on skin, hair or nail scrapings to diagnose fungal infection because KOH:
options: Stains fungal cell walls a distinctive purple colour
Dissolves keratin and host tissue debris, making fungal hyphae/spores easier to visualise under the microscope
Kills the fungal cells so they can be safely handled
Selectively fluoresces fungal elements under UV light
questions.correct_answer: Dissolves keratin and host tissue debris, making fungal hyphae/spores easier to visualise under the microscope
questions.explanation: KOH digests keratinous host material without destroying fungal elements, clearing the background so hyphae and spores are more readily seen by direct microscopy.

questions.question: Amphotericin B exerts its antifungal action by:
options: Binding ergosterol in the fungal cell membrane and forming pores that cause leakage of cell contents
Inhibiting beta-1,3-glucan synthase in the cell wall
questions.correct_answer: Binding ergosterol in the fungal cell membrane and forming pores that cause leakage of cell contents
questions.explanation: Amphotericin B, a polyene, binds ergosterol (the fungal membrane sterol analogous to cholesterol) and forms transmembrane pores, disrupting membrane integrity and causing ion leakage.

questions.question: Azole antifungal drugs (e.g. fluconazole, itraconazole, ketoconazole) act primarily by:
questions.explanation: Azoles inhibit the cytochrome P450 enzyme lanosterol 14α-demethylase, blocking conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol and thereby depleting the fungal membrane of ergosterol.

questions.question: Echinocandins (e.g. caspofungin) are a class of antifungal drugs that act by:
options: Inhibiting beta-1,3-glucan synthase, weakening the fungal cell wall
questions.correct_answer: Inhibiting beta-1,3-glucan synthase, weakening the fungal cell wall
questions.explanation: Echinocandins non-competitively inhibit beta-1,3-glucan synthase, blocking synthesis of glucan, an essential fungal cell wall polysaccharide, leading to osmotic lysis.

questions.question: Griseofulvin, an older oral antifungal used for dermatophytoses, works by:
options: Interfering with fungal microtubule function, inhibiting mitosis, and depositing in newly formed keratin to resist reinfection
questions.correct_answer: Interfering with fungal microtubule function, inhibiting mitosis, and depositing in newly formed keratin to resist reinfection
questions.explanation: Griseofulvin disrupts the mitotic spindle by interacting with fungal microtubules and accumulates in keratin precursor cells, protecting newly formed skin, hair, and nail from dermatophyte invasion.

questions.question: Which yeast species is the workhorse organism of the brewing and baking industries, fermenting sugars to ethanol and carbon dioxide?
questions.explanation: Saccharomyces cerevisiae (baker's/brewer's yeast) ferments hexose sugars to ethanol and CO2, making it central to bread leavening, beer, and wine production.

questions.question: The original industrial source of penicillin, the first mass-produced antibiotic, was the mold:
questions.explanation: Penicillium chrysogenum (a high-yield mutant derived from strains related to P. notatum) has been used industrially for large-scale penicillin fermentation.

questions.question: Aspergillus niger is of major industrial importance chiefly for its large-scale fermentative production of:
questions.explanation: Aspergillus niger is the principal industrial organism used for submerged and surface fermentation production of citric acid, widely used in food, beverage, and pharmaceutical industries.

questions.question: Blue-veined cheeses such as Roquefort and Camembert-style ripening rely on the activity of:
questions.explanation: Penicillium roqueforti gives blue cheeses their characteristic veining and flavour, while Penicillium camemberti forms the white rind and ripens soft cheeses like Camembert and Brie.

questions.question: Tempeh, the traditional Indonesian fermented soybean food, is produced through fermentation by:
questions.explanation: Rhizopus oligosporus mycelium binds cooked, dehulled soybeans into a firm cake during tempeh fermentation, also contributing proteolytic and lipolytic enzyme activity that improves digestibility.

questions.question: Pneumocystis jirovecii, a significant cause of pneumonia in AIDS and other immunocompromised patients, is atypical among pathogenic fungi because it:
options: Lacks ergosterol in its membrane and is resistant to most standard antifungal drugs like amphotericin B and azoles
questions.correct_answer: Lacks ergosterol in its membrane and is resistant to most standard antifungal drugs like amphotericin B and azoles
questions.explanation: Pneumocystis jirovecii membranes are largely cholesterol-based rather than ergosterol-based, so it is intrinsically resistant to amphotericin B and azoles; treatment instead relies on agents like trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.

questions.question: Coccidioidomycosis (Valley Fever), endemic to arid regions of the Americas, is characterised in tissue by the presence of large, thick-walled structures called:
questions.explanation: In host tissue, Coccidioides immitis/posadasii converts to large spherules packed with endospores, a diagnostic tissue form distinct from its mold form in soil.

questions.question: A mycorrhiza is best described as:
options: A disease of fungal origin affecting only cereal crops
A mutualistic symbiotic association between a fungus and the roots of a vascular plant
A type of asexual fungal spore
A fungal infection of the human respiratory tract
questions.correct_answer: A mutualistic symbiotic association between a fungus and the roots of a vascular plant
questions.explanation: Mycorrhizal fungi form mutualistic associations with plant roots, enhancing the plant's water and mineral (especially phosphate) uptake in exchange for photosynthetically fixed carbon.

questions.question: A lichen is fundamentally a symbiotic partnership between a fungus and:
options: A photosynthetic partner, either a green alga or a cyanobacterium
questions.correct_answer: A photosynthetic partner, either a green alga or a cyanobacterium
questions.explanation: Lichens are composite organisms in which a fungal mycobiont associates with a photosynthetic photobiont (green alga and/or cyanobacterium) that supplies fixed carbon and, in cyanobacterial lichens, fixed nitrogen.

questions.question: In fungal asexual reproduction, spores borne exogenously (not enclosed in a sac) at the tips or sides of specialised hyphae, as seen in Aspergillus and Penicillium, are called:
questions.explanation: Conidia are asexual spores produced exogenously (not within an enclosing sporangium) on conidiophores, as typified by Aspergillus and Penicillium.

questions.question: Asexual spores produced endogenously within an enclosed sac called a sporangium, characteristic of Rhizopus and Mucor, are termed:
questions.explanation: Sporangiospores are formed by cleavage of cytoplasm within a sporangium, a hallmark of the Mucoromycota (e.g. Rhizopus, Mucor) reproductive cycle.
